Q5290810.label: 2004 Dominican Republic presidential election
Q5290810.summary: Presidential elections were held in the Dominican Republic on 16 May 2004. The result was a victory for former president Leonel Fernández, who defeated incumbent Hipólito Mejía. Voter turnout was 72.8%.

Q19876154.label: Thirty-fourth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q19876154.desc: amendment to permit marriage to be contracted by two persons without distinction as to their sex
aliases: 34th Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q19876154.wiki: Thirty-fourth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q19876154.img: Election badges promoting a "yes" vote from Ireland's Marriage Equality referendum in 2015.jpg
Q19876154.summary: The Thirty-fourth Amendment of the Constitution Act 2015 amended the Constitution of Ireland to permit marriage to be contracted by two persons without distinction as to their sex. Prior to the enactment, the Constitution was assumed to contain an implicit prohibition on same-sex marriage in Ireland.

Q949562.label: Polish European Union membership referendum
Q949562.summary: A referendum on joining the European Union was held in Poland on 7 and 8 June 2003. The proposal was approved by 77% of voters. Poland subsequently joined the European Union that year following the ratification of the Treaty of Accession 2003. The country's first European Parliament elections were held in 2004.

Q171834.label: Aldo Moro
Q171834.summary: Aldo Moro was an Italian statesman and prominent member of Christian Democracy (DC) and its centre-left wing. He served as prime minister of Italy for five terms from December 1963 to June 1968 and from November 1974 to July 1976.

Q384826.label: Reform Party
Q384826.summary: The Reform Party, formerly known as Zatlers' Reform Party until April 2012, was a centre-right political party in Latvia founded by former President Valdis Zatlers on 23 July 2011. It won 22 seats in the Saeima in the 2011 election.

Q4393786.label: Latvian citizenship referendum, 1998
Q4393786.summary: A referendum on the citizenship law was held in Latvia on 3 October 1998. The Saeima had made amendments to the law in June that increased the opportunities for naturalisation and provided the additional option of obtaining Latvian citizenship for non-citizens (nepilsoņi) and stateless persons (bezvalstnieki) born in Latvia from August 1991 onwards.

Q4808506.label: assassination of Erkut Akbay
Q4808506.summary: The assassination of Erkut Akbay refers to the murder of the Turkish administrative attache, Erkut Akbay, 40, in Lisbon, where the diplomat was serving, on 7 June 1982. Akbay was assassinated near his home on the outskirts of the city as he returned home for lunch with his wife.

Q694586.label: Solingen arson attack of 1993
Q694586.desc: neo-nazi arson attack on Turkish home in Solingen
Q694586.summary: The Solingen arson attack was one of the most severe instances of racist violence in modern Germany. On the night of 28–29 May 1993, four young German men belonging to the far right skinhead scene, with neo-Nazi ties, set fire to the house of a large Turkish family in the city of Solingen, in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

Q40355642.label: 2017 Central Mexico earthquake
Q40355642.summary: The 2017 Puebla earthquake, also known as 19S, struck at 13:14 CDT on 19 September 2017 with an estimated magnitude of 7.1 Mw and strong shaking for about 20 seconds. Its epicenter was about 55 km (34 mi) south of the city of Puebla, Mexico.

Q108902202.label: murder of David Amess
Q108902202.desc: 2021 killing of a UK member of parliament
Q108902202.summary: On 15 October 2021, David Amess, a British Conservative Party politician and Member of Parliament for Southend West, was fatally stabbed at a constituency surgery at Belfairs Methodist Church Hall in Leigh-on-Sea, Essex. His killer, Ali Harbi Ali, a British citizen and Islamic State sympathiser, was arrested at the scene.

Q38352698.label: ultranationalism
Q38352698.summary: Ultranationalism, or extreme nationalism, is an extremist form of nationalism in which a country asserts or maintains hegemony, supremacy, or other forms of control over other nations, to pursue its specific interests. Ultranationalist entities have been associated with the engagement of political violence even during peacetime.

Q826.label: Maldives
Q826.desc: sovereign state in South Asia, situated on an archipelago in the Arabian Sea
Q826.summary: The Maldives, officially the Republic of Maldives, and historically known as the Maldive Islands, is an archipelagic country in South Asia, located in the Indian Ocean, near the southeastern boundary of the Arabian Sea. The Maldives is located southwest of India and Sri Lanka, about 750 kilometres from the Asian continent's mainland. The Maldives' chain of 26 atolls stretches across the equator from Ihavandhippolhu Atoll in the north to Addu Atoll in the south.
